home.title: Calculators for Armenia
home.description: Work out net salary, sole proprietor tax, car import customs, currency conversion and money transfer fees under the rules in force.
home.heading: Calculators for Armenia
home.intro: Plain calculations from the official rules. Every value cites its source.

salary.title: Armenia Salary Tax Calculator {year}
salary.description: Work out take-home pay in Armenia for {year}: income tax at {rate}, pension contribution, stamp payment and health insurance. Step-by-step breakdown with links to the law.
salary.intro: Enter a gross monthly salary and this gross-to-net calculator shows the net pay left after every mandatory withholding: income tax, the funded pension contribution, the stamp payment and the health insurance premium. Every figure comes from the law, and the sources are listed at the foot of the page.

calculator.grossHint: The amount before tax, as written in the employment contract.
calculator.pensionHint: Mandatory for employees born on or after 1 January 1974.
calculator.regimeHint: The reduced rate applies only to staff engaged in R&D work with a positive opinion from the professional commission.
calculator.jsNote: The result updates as you change the amount.

howItWorks.heading: How take-home pay is calculated
howItWorks.intro: All four withholdings are taken from the gross salary. One detail matters: the pension contribution, stamp payment and health premium do not reduce the income tax base, so income tax is charged on the whole gross amount.
steps: Income tax: {rate} of gross salary.

Funded pension contribution: {pensionLowerRate} where salary is up to {pensionLowerBandMax}; above that, {pensionUpperRate} minus {pensionDeduction}. The base is capped at {pensionCap} (15 times the {minWage} minimum wage), so the contribution can never exceed {pensionMax}.
Stamp payment: {stampLow} where salary is up to {stampThreshold}, and {stampHigh} above it.

Health insurance: {healthReduced} where salary runs from {healthNoneNext} to {healthReducedMax}, with the state paying the rest, and {healthFull} above that. Employees earning up to {healthNone} have nothing withheld in {year}.
Take-home pay = gross salary minus those four amounts.
howItWorks.note: Rounding: no rounding rule was found in any of the laws, so the calculator does not round intermediate amounts.

examples.heading: Worked examples
examples.intro: Three typical salaries. These run through the same code as the calculator above.

items.q: How much tax is withheld from a salary in Armenia in {year}?
items.a: Four payments come out of a salary: income tax at {rate}, the funded pension contribution, the stamp payment and the health insurance premium. The total depends on the amount: on a salary of {exampleLowGross} the take-home pay is {exampleLowNet}, and on {exampleMidGross} it is {exampleMidNet}.

items.q: What is the income tax rate in Armenia?
items.a: {rate}. It is a flat rate with no progressive scale and no tax-free allowance, in force since 1 January 2023. Before that it stepped down year by year: 23% in 2020, 22% in 2021 and 21% in 2022.

items.q: What is the stamp payment and how much is it?
items.a: It funds compensation for injured servicemen. From 1 January {year} it is {stampLow} a month where salary is up to {stampThreshold}, and {stampHigh} above that. It used to be a five-step scale from 1,500 to 15,000 dram, so if another site shows those figures, it is out of date.

items.q: Who pays the funded pension contribution?
items.a: It is mandatory for employees born on or after 1 January 1974. Those born earlier may opt in voluntarily, but the choice cannot be reversed. The rate is {pensionLowerRate} on salary up to {pensionLowerBandMax}, and {pensionUpperRate} minus {pensionDeduction} above that. The state adds up to {pensionDeduction} a month to your account, and that top-up does not reduce your take-home pay.

items.q: Why does the pension contribution stop growing on a high salary?
items.a: The base is capped at 15 times the minimum monthly wage. With the minimum wage at {minWage}, that cap is {pensionCap} a month. Nothing is charged on the excess, so the contribution tops out at {pensionMax} however much you earn. If you have more than one job, the cap applies to your combined income from all employers.

items.q: What is the {healthReduced} and {healthFull} health insurance premium?
items.a: The full premium is {healthFull} a month. On a salary from {healthNoneNext} to {healthReducedMax} the employee pays {healthReduced} and the state budget covers the rest. Above {healthReducedMax} the employee pays the whole premium. On a salary up to {healthNone}, nothing is withheld in {year} yet.

items.q: Do IT workers really pay {rdRate} instead of {rate}?
items.a: A reduced {rdRate} rate exists, but it is not the one usually described. The relief for companies holding an IT certificate ended on 31 December 2024. Since 2025 a different relief applies, for staff engaged in research and development, conditional on a positive opinion from the professional commission and on the occupation appearing in the government's high-tech list. It is legislated to run to the end of 2031.

items.q: What changes in 2027?
items.a: Under the adopted text of the law, the reduced {healthReduced} employee share ends on 1 January 2027: every employee will pay the full {healthFull}, including those earning up to {healthNone}. A draft amendment that would keep the reduced share was under discussion in autumn {year}, but it had not been adopted when this data was verified.

sources.heading: Sources
sources.intro: Every value in the calculator is taken from the law as currently consolidated. Here is what came from where.

disclaimer.heading: Please note
disclaimer.text: This is an advisory calculation, not tax advice, and not a substitute for your payslip. Your employer's withholdings may differ — for instance if you hold more than one job, started mid-month, or have a court-ordered deduction.
caveats: The pension cap is assessed on income from all employers combined. The calculator sees one salary, so it can overstate the contribution for someone with more than one job.

For {year} the law says the {healthReduced} health premium is paid by the tax agent. That it comes out of the employee's own pay is confirmed by published guidance rather than by the wording of the law itself.
The law does not state which month's salary decides between the {healthReduced} and {healthFull} share. The calculator uses the current month's salary from that employer.

entrepreneur.title: Armenia Individual Entrepreneur Tax Calculator {year}
entrepreneur.description: Work out what an individual entrepreneur (sole proprietor) pays in Armenia in {year}: turnover tax by activity, the micro-enterprise regime, the fixed {fixedProfitTaxMonthly} a month, pension, stamp payment and health insurance. Step by step, with links to the law.
entrepreneur.intro: Choose a regime and an activity, enter a year's turnover, and see what an individual entrepreneur (sole proprietor) in Armenia pays: turnover tax, the fixed profit tax, the pension payment, the stamp payment and health insurance. Every rate comes from the Tax Code and the laws in force; the sources are listed at the foot of the page.

calculator.regimeHint: Turnover tax is open up to {turnoverThreshold} of turnover a year, the micro-enterprise regime up to {microThreshold}. Above that, the general regime with VAT applies.
calculator.activityHint: Sets the turnover tax rate. The {rateIt} rate applies only to activities on the government's high-technology list.
calculator.turnoverHint: All sales revenue for the year, before expenses.
calculator.expensesHint: Reduce turnover tax for services, trade, production and catering. They must be documented; buying fixed assets does not count.
calculator.pensionHint: Mandatory for anyone born on or after 1 January 1974.
calculator.resultLabel: Left after tax for the year

warnings.overTurnoverThreshold: Above {turnoverThreshold} of turnover, turnover tax is not available: the entrepreneur moves to the general regime with VAT.
warnings.overMicroThreshold: Above {microThreshold} of turnover, the micro-enterprise regime is not available.
warnings.microExcluded: The micro-enterprise regime is closed to this activity: it excludes trade, software development and income from rent, interest and royalties.

howItWorks.heading: How individual entrepreneur tax is calculated in Armenia
howItWorks.intro: The calculator works over a full year. What an entrepreneur pays is a tax on the business itself, which depends on the regime, plus mandatory payments that almost everyone makes.
steps: Turnover tax: the rate for the activity times the year's turnover. That is {rateServices} for services, {rateTrade} for trade, {rateProduction} for production, {rateCatering} for catering and {rateIt} for IT on the high-tech list.

Expenses: the tax falls by {creditServices} of documented expenses for services, {creditTrade} for trade, {creditProduction} for production and {creditCatering} for catering. It cannot fall below a minimum: {minServices} of turnover for services, {minTrade} for trade, {minProduction} for production and {minCatering} for catering.
Fixed profit tax: {fixedProfitTaxMonthly} a month, or {fixedProfitTaxYear} a year. Only entrepreneurs on turnover tax pay it.
Pension contribution: {turnoverPensionMonthly} a month ({turnoverPensionYear} a year) on turnover tax. A micro-enterprise pays {microPensionRate} of income.
Stamp payment: {stampLow} a year for turnover up to {stampThreshold}, and {stampHigh} above that.
Health insurance: {healthPremium} a year if last year's income was above {healthThreshold}.
Left after tax = turnover minus all of the above. Business expenses are not subtracted from this figure.
howItWorks.note: A micro-enterprise pays no turnover tax, profit tax or VAT on its micro income, only the mandatory payments. The calculator does not cover the general regime (profit tax at {generalRate} and VAT at {vatRate}), because the result there depends on deductions and input VAT.

examples.heading: Worked examples
examples.intro: An IT freelancer at {rateIt}, a services business with expenses and a small workshop on the micro-enterprise regime. Each is run through the same code as the calculator above.

items.q: How much tax does an individual entrepreneur pay in Armenia in {year}?
items.a: It depends on the regime and the activity. An IT entrepreneur at {rateIt} with {exampleItTurnover} of turnover pays {exampleItTotal} for the year, all mandatory payments included. A services business with {exampleServicesTurnover} of turnover and {exampleServicesExpenses} of expenses pays {exampleServicesTotal}. A micro-enterprise with {exampleMicroTurnover} of turnover pays {exampleMicroTotal}.

items.q: What is the turnover tax rate in Armenia in {year}?
items.a: Since 1 January 2025: services and other activities {rateServices}, trade {rateTrade}, production {rateProduction}, catering {rateCatering}, rent, interest and royalties {rateRent}, and high-technology activities on the government list {rateIt}. Before 2025 the rates were lower, for example 5% for services and trade, which is why older sites quote different figures.

items.q: Do IT sole proprietors really pay {rateIt}?
items.a: Yes, if the activity is on the government's high-technology list. The rate runs until the end of {itRateUntilYear}. IT work not on the list is taxed as other services, at {rateServices}. On top of the tax, the entrepreneur pays {fixedProfitTaxYear} a year of fixed profit tax and the mandatory payments, so the real burden is above {rateIt}.

items.q: Who can use the micro-enterprise regime?
items.a: An entrepreneur or company whose turnover last year was no more than {microThreshold}. It is closed to trade, software development, consulting, legal, accounting, design, marketing and many other services, and to anyone receiving rent, interest or royalties. A micro-enterprise pays no turnover tax or profit tax, but does pay the {microPensionRate} pension contribution, the stamp payment and health insurance.

items.q: How do expenses reduce turnover tax?
items.a: For services, trade, production and catering the tax falls by a share of documented expenses: {creditServices} of them for services. It never falls below the minimum, which is {minServices} of turnover for services. Fixed assets, business travel and entertainment do not count. The unused part carries forward to later periods; the calculator covers one year and leaves that out.

items.q: General regime or turnover tax: which is better for a sole proprietor?
items.a: Under the general regime an entrepreneur pays profit tax at {generalRate} on income minus deductions, plus VAT at {vatRate}. It can pay off with large documented costs or clients who need a VAT invoice. Turnover tax is simpler and usually cheaper when costs are low. Above {turnoverThreshold} of turnover there is no choice: the general regime applies.

items.q: What does a sole proprietor pay besides the tax?
items.a: The pension contribution: {turnoverPensionMonthly} a month on turnover tax, if you were born on or after 1 January 1974. The stamp payment: {stampLow} or {stampHigh} a year depending on turnover. And from {year}, health insurance of {healthPremium} a year if last year's income was above {healthThreshold}.

items.q: What changes for entrepreneurs in {nextYear}?
items.a: From 1 January {nextYear}, every entrepreneur pays the {healthPremium} health insurance premium, including those with income up to {healthThreshold}. E-commerce platform operators lose access to turnover tax and the micro-enterprise regime. No change to the {microThreshold} and {turnoverThreshold} thresholds had been adopted when the data was checked.

sources.heading: Sources
sources.intro: Every value in the calculator comes from the Tax Code and the laws as currently in force. Here is where each one comes from.

disclaimer.heading: Important
disclaimer.text: This is an estimate, not tax advice. What you actually pay depends on when you registered, whether you suspended activity and which activities you carry out.
caveats: The calculator covers a full year. Fixed payments accrue by month, so they are lower if you registered mid-year.
Health insurance depends on last year's income. The calculator assumes it equalled this year's turnover.
The law does not say outright what counts as "income" for the micro-enterprise pension contribution ({microPensionRate}). The calculator uses all turnover.
The {rateIt} rate applies only to activities on the government's high-technology list; we have not checked the list itself.
With several activities, turnover tax is calculated for each one separately. The calculator handles one.

car-customs.title: Armenia Car Customs Clearance Calculator {year}
car-customs.description: Work out the customs payments on a car imported into Armenia in {year}: the unified payment for individuals, duty and {vatRate} VAT for companies, electric cars and hybrids, and the environmental tax. Step by step at the central bank rate, with links to the law.
car-customs.intro: Say who is importing and from where, then the car's fuel, year, engine size and price, and this car import duty calculator shows every customs payment for bringing it into Armenia: the unified payment or the duty, VAT and the environmental tax. It covers cars from the USA, Georgia, the UAE, China, Europe and the EAEU. Rates come from the EAEU customs tariff and the Armenian Tax Code; the sources are listed at the foot of the page.

calculator.situationHint: "Outside the EAEU" means the USA, Georgia, the UAE, China, Europe and so on. For a car already cleared in Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan or Kyrgyzstan, pick an EAEU option.

situations.personal: Individual, for own use, outside the EAEU
situations.eaeuFirst: Individual, from the EAEU, first car this year
situations.eaeu: From the EAEU: company or second car

calculator.fuelHint: For an individual, a hybrid is charged like a petrol car of the same engine size.
calculator.yearHint: Age runs from the production date to the day the customs declaration is filed.
calculator.monthHint: If the month is unknown, customs treats the car as made on 1 July.
calculator.ccHint: In cubic centimetres, as in the registration papers. Not needed for an electric car.
calculator.priceHint: The customs value for a car from outside the EAEU; the purchase price for a car from the EAEU.
calculator.currencyHint: Converted at the Central Bank of Armenia rate of {rateDate}: €1 = {eurRate}, $1 = {usdRate}.

warnings.hybridAssumed: The hybrid is charged {hybridPercent}, as the official calculator does. If the combustion engine is more powerful than the electric motor, duty follows the petrol or diesel table instead.
warnings.eaeuEnvUnconfirmed: No source confirms whether the first car of the year is exempt from the environmental tax, so it is included.

howItWorks.heading: How car customs in Armenia are calculated
howItWorks.intro: What you pay depends first on who imports the car and where it comes from. Each case has its own rules.
steps: An individual importing for their own use from outside the EAEU pays one unified payment that already includes VAT. For a car up to 3 years old it is {unifiedPercent} of the value ({unifiedLowPercent} for cars under {unifiedLowMax}), but not less than a minimum in euros per cubic centimetre. For an older car the value does not matter: the payment is a euro rate times the engine size.

A company importing from outside the EAEU pays EAEU tariff duty: {tariffNewPercent} for cars up to 3 years old, {tariffUsedPercent} (but not less than a per-cm³ minimum) for 3 to 7 years, and a per-cm³ rate for older cars. VAT of {vatRate} is then charged on the value plus the duty.
An electric car pays {evPercent} duty at any age, even for an individual, plus VAT. In {year} there is no VAT if the car was made after {evMadeAfter}.
A car from an EAEU country pays no duty. VAT is {vatRate} of the purchase price, except on an individual's first car of the year. It is paid to the tax authority by the 20th of the following month.
Everyone pays the environmental tax: {env1} of the value for cars up to 3 years old, {env2} for 3 to 5, {env3} for 5 to 10, {env4} for 10 to 15 and {env5} above 15 years.
Euros are converted to drams at the Central Bank of Armenia rate on the day the declaration is filed. The calculator uses the rate of {rateDate}: €1 = {eurRate}, $1 = {usdRate}, ₽1 = {rubRate}.
howItWorks.note: On top of these: the state fee for the declaration, {stateDutyPassenger} for an individual and {stateDutyGoods} for a company, and registration with the road police. Armenia charges no excise on passenger cars.

examples.heading: Worked examples
examples.intro: Three cars an individual brings in for their own use from outside the EAEU: an older petrol car, a recent hybrid and an electric car. Calculated for {rateDate} at that day's central bank rate, with the same code as the calculator above.

items.q: How much is customs for a car in Armenia in {year}?
items.a: It depends on the car's age, engine size and, for cars up to 3 years old, its value. A {ex1Year} petrol car with a {ex1Cc} cm³ engine priced at {ex1Price} pays {ex1Total} in customs payments. A {ex2Year} hybrid at {ex2Price} pays {ex2Total}. A {ex3Year} electric car at {ex3Price} pays {ex3Total}.

items.q: How is customs different for an individual and a company?
items.a: An individual bringing in one car for their own use pays a unified customs payment that already includes both duty and VAT. A company pays EAEU tariff duty and, separately, {vatRate} VAT. Which works out cheaper depends on the car's age, engine and price, so run both in the calculator. Both pay the environmental tax.

items.q: What is the import duty on an electric car in Armenia in {year}?
items.a: Electric cars get no unified payment, even for individuals: duty is {evPercent} of the value, plus {vatRate} VAT. In {year} there is no VAT if the car was made after {evMadeAfter}; the exemption runs until {evExemptTo}. A zero-duty quota runs until {evQuotaTo}, but customs reported that the share for individuals ran out on {evQuotaClosed}, so the calculator charges {evPercent}. The environmental tax applies.

items.q: How is a hybrid cleared through customs in Armenia?
items.a: An individual pays the unified payment on the combustion engine's size, exactly as for a petrol car. A company pays {hybridPercent} duty if the electric motor is more powerful than the combustion engine, and the petrol or diesel table otherwise. The official customs calculator does not ask about power and always uses {hybridPercent}.

items.q: Is it different importing a car from the USA, Georgia, Dubai or China?
items.a: No. The same rules apply to every country outside the EAEU: what matters is the car's age, engine size and value, and who imports it. The country only affects the customs value: for a company it includes shipping and insurance to the Armenian border.

items.q: Do I pay customs on a car from Russia or another EAEU country?
items.a: If the car is already cleared in an EAEU country, there is no duty and no customs declaration. You still pay {vatRate} VAT on the purchase price (an individual's first car of the year is exempt) and the environmental tax, to the tax authority, by the 20th of the following month.

items.q: What is the environmental tax on an imported car?
items.a: It is a one-off tax on importing a car that depends on its age: {env1} of the value up to 3 years, {env2} up to 5, {env3} up to 10, {env4} up to 15 and {env5} above that. This scale has applied since 1 June 2024; older pages show different rates.

items.q: Can I calculate customs for taking a car from Armenia to Russia here?
items.a: No. Taking a car from Armenia into Russia follows Russian rules, including the recycling fee. This calculator only covers importing a car into Armenia.

sources.heading: Sources
sources.intro: Every value in the calculator comes from the EAEU customs tariff, EEC decisions, the Armenian Tax Code and customs guidance. Here is where each one comes from.

labels.unifiedNew: Unified payment: cars up to 3 years old
labels.unifiedOld: Unified payment: cars over 5 years old

disclaimer.heading: Important
disclaimer.text: This is an estimate, not customs advice. Customs decides the customs value and may not accept the price you declare.
caveats: The central bank rate is that of {rateDate}, updated every business day. Customs applies the rate on the day the declaration is filed, so the result can differ slightly.

For an individual, the EAEU Customs Code leaves shipping and insurance out of the customs value, while Armenian customs guidance includes them up to the border. This affects cars up to 3 years old and the environmental tax.
The calculator does not cover special-purpose off-road vehicles, motorhomes, special vehicles or customs' reference values.

currency.title: USD to AMD Converter at the Central Bank of Armenia Rate
currency.description: Convert dollars, euros, rubles and other currencies ({currencyCount} in all) to Armenian drams at the official Central Bank of Armenia rate of {rateDate}: $1 = {usdRate}. Updated every business day.
currency.h1: USD to AMD converter: dram, dollar, euro and ruble
currency.intro: Enter an amount and pick two currencies: the converter uses the Central Bank of Armenia rate of {rateDate}, taken straight from the central bank and updated every business day. Banks and exchange offices use their own rates; the difference is explained below.

calculator.amountHint: A whole number, in the currency you convert from.
calculator.fromHint: Central Bank of Armenia rate of {rateDate}: $1 = {usdRate}, €1 = {eurRate}, ₽1 = {rubRate}.
calculator.toHint: A pair without the dram is converted through the dram, using two central bank rates.

howItWorks.heading: How the conversion works
howItWorks.intro: The Central Bank of Armenia publishes the dram's rate against each currency, and every conversion goes through it.
steps: The central bank rate is the average rate formed on the currency market. The central bank publishes it every business day, and this page takes it straight from the central bank.
From a currency into drams: amount × rate. At $1 = {usdRate}, {ex2Amount} is {ex2Result}.
From drams into a currency: amount ÷ rate.
Between two other currencies, through the dram: amount × the first rate ÷ the second. So {ex3Amount} is {ex3Result}.
Some rates are quoted for more than one unit: per 10 for the {per10}, per 100 for the {per100}. The calculator converts them to one unit.
howItWorks.note: This is the official reference rate. Banks and exchange offices buy below it and sell above it. For the cost of a transfer including the bank's fee, use the transfer fees calculator.

examples.heading: Worked examples
examples.intro: Three common conversions at the central bank rate of {rateDate}, run through the same code as the converter above.

items.q: What is the USD to AMD rate today?
items.a: At the Central Bank of Armenia rate of {rateDate}, $1 = {usdRate}, so {ex2Amount} is {ex2Result}. The euro is €1 = {eurRate} and the ruble ₽1 = {rubRate}.

items.q: Why does my bank give a different rate?
items.a: The central bank rate is the market average. Banks buy currency below it and sell above it, and the gap is their margin. On {snapshotDate}, {bankCount} large banks bought non-cash dollars {usdBuyRange} below the central bank rate. For the full cost of a transfer including the bank's fee, use the transfer fees calculator.

items.q: Why are cash rubles exchanged at a worse rate?
items.a: Banks pay much less for cash rubles than for rubles on an account. On {snapshotDate}, {bankCount} large banks bought cash rubles {rubCashBuyRange} below the central bank rate, against {rubCashlessBuyRange} for non-cash rubles. Bank rates move several times a day.

items.q: How often is the rate updated?
items.a: The central bank publishes a new rate every business day. There is none on weekends and holidays, when the last published rate stays in force. This page fetches the rate from the central bank twice a day, and the calculator shows its date.

items.q: How do I convert dollars to rubles?
items.a: Through the dram: divide the dollar rate by the ruble rate. On {rateDate}, $1 = {usdRate} and ₽1 = {rubRate}, so $1 = {usdInRub} and {ex3Amount} is {ex3Result}.

items.q: Which rate does customs use?
items.a: The Central Bank of Armenia rate on the day the declaration is filed. The car customs calculator on this site uses the same rate as this converter.

items.q: Which currencies can I convert?
items.a: All {currencyCount} currencies the Central Bank of Armenia publishes a rate for: besides the dollar, euro and ruble, for example the lari, the dirham, the yuan and the tenge.

sources.heading: Sources
sources.intro: Rates come straight from the Central Bank of Armenia. Bank rates for the cash and non-cash ruble comparison come from the banks' sites, on one day.
sources.what: What the central bank rate is

disclaimer.heading: Important
disclaimer.text: This is a conversion at the official rate, not an exchange offer. A bank or exchange office will use its own rate.
caveats: The rate is the central bank's of {rateDate}; it publishes a new one every business day.
Bank rates in the answers above are from {snapshotDate}; they move several times a day.
Amounts are rounded to the cent.

transfers.title: Send Money to Armenia: Fees and Exchange Rates Compared {year}
transfers.description: What sending money to or from Armenia really costs: the bank fee plus the exchange margin. {bankCount} of the largest banks compared for dollars, euros and rubles, step by step, with links to their tariffs.
transfers.h1: Send money to Armenia and abroad: fees compared
transfers.intro: A bank charges for a transfer twice: the fee, and the gap in its exchange rate, which often costs more. Pick a direction, a currency and an amount, and this calculator ranks {bankCount} of Armenia's largest banks by the full cost of the transfer, cheapest first.

calculator.directionHint: Sending: you pay in drams, the bank buys the currency and sends it by SWIFT. Receiving: money arrives in an Armenian account and you change it into drams.
calculator.currencyHint: Central Bank of Armenia rate of {rateDate}: $1 = {usdRate}, €1 = {eurRate}, ₽1 = {rubRate}.
calculator.baseLabel: Amount at the central bank rate

howItWorks.heading: How the cost of a transfer is worked out
howItWorks.intro: The full cost of a transfer is the bank's fee plus what you lose on the exchange. The calculator works out both in drams and adds them up.
steps: The amount is converted to drams at the Central Bank of Armenia rate. That is the reference point.

Fee: a percentage of the amount, with the minimum and maximum from the bank's tariff. Sending uses the bank's online SWIFT tariff from an account; receiving uses its fee for crediting an incoming transfer.

Exchange margin: when you send, the bank sells you the currency above the central bank rate; when you receive, it buys it below. That gap is a hidden fee. For dollars received it is {usdBuyRange} depending on the bank, for rubles {rubBuyRange}.
Cost of the transfer = fee + amount at the central bank rate × the margin. Banks are listed from cheapest to most expensive.
howItWorks.note: Bank rates were captured once, on {rateDate}, and move several times a day. Fee tariffs change a few times a year. No bank publishes the charges of intermediary banks, so they are not included.

examples.heading: Worked examples
examples.intro: Three typical transfers at the rates of {rateDate}, run through the same code as the calculator above.

items.q: How much does it cost to send money abroad from Armenia?
items.a: For a SWIFT transfer of {ex1Amount} on {rateDate}, the lowest full cost was {ex1Cost} ({ex1Bank}), fee and exchange margin together. The most expensive of the {bankCount} banks would have charged {ex1WorstCost} for the same transfer.

items.q: What are the fees for receiving money in Armenia?
items.a: Most banks credit an incoming transfer to an account for free, or publish no fee for it. Armeconombank charges {aebIncomingLow} to {aebIncomingHigh} depending on the amount. The main cost is the exchange rate: receiving {ex2Amount} and changing it into drams cost from {ex2Cost} ({ex2Bank}) to {ex2WorstCost}.

items.q: Why does the exchange rate matter more than the fee?
items.a: The fee is in the tariff; the rate gap is not. Banks buy dollars from you {usdBuyRange} below the central bank rate, and rubles {rubBuyRange} below. On a large amount that gap easily exceeds the fee, so compare banks on the full cost of the transfer.

items.q: How do I send money from Armenia to Russia?
items.a: In rubles is cheapest: banks charge a small percentage with a minimum, and Ardshinbank a flat {ardshinRubFee}. For {ex3Amount}, the lowest cost including the exchange margin was {ex3Cost} ({ex3Bank}). Many banks will not send dollars or euros to Russia, or charge far more: ACBA Bank's minimum is {acbaToRussiaMin}, Armeconombank's {aebToRussiaMin}.

items.q: Which services send money to Armenia from Russia?
items.a: Unistream sends transfers to Armenia paid out in cash in rubles; paying with a Unistream card, the fee is {unistreamRate}. KoronaPay's status is unclear: its official site shows us only its European branch's notice, so we do not quote its fees. Once rubles reach an Armenian account, mind the bank's exchange rate, which the calculator covers.

items.q: How do I send money to Armenia from the US or Europe?
items.a: Wise pays out in drams to an Armenian bank account. On {rateDate}, sending {wiseAmount} from the US cost {wiseFee} in fees, and Wise's rate was slightly better than the central bank's. Wise prices change constantly, so treat this as an example, not a tariff. Western Union does not offer online transfers to Armenia.

items.q: Why is Inecobank not in the comparison?
items.a: Inecobank's website blocks automated access with a Cloudflare check, and we did not get around it. No official tariff was found publicly, so the bank is left out.

items.q: How often is this data updated?
items.a: Bank rates move several times a day, so the calculator holds a snapshot from {rateDate}. Fee tariffs change a few times a year. Check the rate in your bank's app before you transfer.

sources.heading: Sources
sources.intro: Fees come from the banks' official tariffs, and rates from the banks' sites and the Central Bank of Armenia on the same day. Below is each bank's tariff for sending dollars abroad.

disclaimer.heading: Important
disclaimer.text: This is a reference comparison, not financial advice. Check the rate and the fee with your bank before you transfer.
caveats: Bank rates are a snapshot from {rateDate}; they move several times a day.

Banks split intermediary charges differently: some have the sender pay them, others take them out of the amount. The calculator uses each bank's main online tariff; intermediary charges are not included.
Tariffs are for residents sending from their own account. Fees are higher for non-residents and for transfers without an account.
Where a bank publishes no fee for crediting an incoming transfer, the calculator counts only the exchange margin.
